case_name: Shahu Shikshan Prasarak Mandal And Anr. v Lata P. Kore & Ors
petitioner: Shahu Shikshan Prasarak Mandal And Anr
facts: Challenge in this appeal is to the order of a Division Bench of the Bombay High Court dismissing the Letters Patent Appeal filed by the appellant.
Writ Petition filed by the appellant was dismissed on the ground that the same was not maintainable.
Learned counsel for the respondent on the other hand supported the impugned judgment of the High Court.
Rules 3, 18(41) and the proviso 18(44) read as follows:
In Umaji Keshao Meshram v. Radhikabai , Sushilabai Laxminarayan Mudliyar & Ors. v. Nihalchand Waghajibhai Shaha & Ors.
In Sushilabai's case (supra) it was noted as follows:
The Full Bench of the Bombay High Court wrongly understood the above Umaji Kesho Meshram case.
All this suggests that the writ petition was not only u/art. 227 of the Constitution Of India, 1950 but there is a specific mention of Article 226.
In a reported decision of this Court in Sushilabai Laxminarayan Mudliyar & Ors. V. Nihalchand Waghajibhai Shaha and others a similar question fell for consideration.
The effect of the provisions and the decisions referred to above does not appear to have been considered by the High Court while holding that the Letters Patent Appeal was not maintainable.
issues: Whether an appeal would lie from the decision of the Single Judge in such a case.
petitioner_arguments: The impugned order of the Division Bench is clearly unsustainable.
Reference is made to Rules 3 & 18 of the Bombay High Court Appellate Side Rules, 1960 with the amended Letters Patent of the High Court of Bombay, 1865 .
It is submitted that the Division Bench did not take note of what has been stated by several judgments of this Court.
respondent_arguments: Rules 3, 18(41) and the proviso 18(44) read as follows:
The Full Bench of the Bombay High Court wrongly understood the above Umaji Kesho Meshram case.
court_reasoning: In our opinion, where the facts justify a party in filing an application either u/art. 226 or 227 of the Constitution Of India, 1950, and the party chooses to file his application under both these articles, in fairness and justice to such party and in order not to deprive him of the valuable right of appeal the court ought to treat the application as being made under Article 226, and if in deciding the matter, in the final order the court gives ancillary directions which may pertain to Article 227, this ought not to be held to deprive a party of the right of appeal u/cl. 15 of the Letters Patent where the substantial part of the order sought to be appealed against is under Article 226.
holding: In these circumstances we set aside the impugned order of the Division Bench and direct that the Letters Patent Appeal filed against the judgment of the learned Single Judge would now be heard and decided on merits.
The appeals are allowed in part with no order as to costs.
